title: Rapid API Adoption Path - Discovery
summary: Introductory discovery focused on fast time-to-first-token for self-serve Redwood API, tradeoffs between Hosted/Dedicated/Private, and security/compliance concerns for an enterprise analytics platform. Team asked for sandbox credits, security docs (SSO/SAML, KMS), and a short benchmark plan. Agreed next step: 2-week sandbox + 48h sizing follow-up call.

security: SOC2, KMS, SSO/SAML, VPC connectivity
performance and latency expectations for embeddings and chat
next_steps: Redwood to provision 2-week sandbox with $2k credits and send onboarding checklist
SE to share benchmarking template and runbook within 48 hours
Schedule follow-up call for sizing and pilot scope in 7 business days

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-06-11 14:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Leo Garcia (Redwood SE), Ivy Park (Redwood CSM); Aisha Patel (Head of ML, Nimbus), Tom Reeves (Platform Eng), Samir Das (CTO), Riley (Data Scientist)

Summary (auto): quick discovery: want to get devs playing with the API rapidly, consider hosted for speed but worried about data residency and audit logs; dedicated or private if pilot requires steady throughput and SOC2 controls.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick intros and then jump into what you're trying to accomplish, is that right Aisha?
[00:15] Aisha Patel: yeah thanks Maya, we have about 25 minutes of agenda, we want to understand time to first token for our engineers, and whether we should start on Hosted or jump straight to Dedicated. Also security is a hard requirement for us.
[00:30] Leo Garcia: cool, I'll do a quick tech overview, but high level: Redwood's hosted API gets you to tokens within minutes — SDKs, sample apps, free credits — Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation, Private gives VPC/air-gapped options.
[00:45] Tom Reeves: when you say "minutes" like does that assume we already have an account and API key or is there an enterprise provisioning step?
[00:55] Maya Chen: good question, for self-serve it's literally sign up, get free credits, and you can call the endpoints — so literally time-to-first-token in an hour incl. onboarding. For enterprise we can accelerate via invite links and pre-provisioned credits.
[01:20] Samir Das: our concern is auditability and KMS. We need customer-managed keys for anything PII. Hosted usually means you manage keys?
[01:30] Leo Garcia: right, for Hosted we offer envelope encryption and we can integrate with your KMS for Dedicated and Private; Hosted by default uses Redwood-managed KMS but we have bring-your-own-KMS options on Dedicated and Private tiers. sometimes docs call it "KMSs" — sorry the doc typo — but yes BYOK on Dedicated.
[01:55] Riley: also curious about tokenization latency for embeddings, we plan to embed millions of records, so cost and throughput matter.
[02:05] Leo Garcia: embeddings are a good example — Hosted is cheaper to start, but for large volume Dedicated often reduces unit cost and gives reserved throughput. We do automatic batching and KV prefix cache optimizations which cut CPU/GPU cost for repeated prefixes.
[02:30] Aisha Patel: can you explain the KV caching bit in plain english, we have a couple of model types — retrieval augmented generation and vector search — what's the implication?
[02:45] Leo Garcia: sure, KV cache basically stores recent decoder states to avoid recomputing attention for tokens already processed, so for chat-like workloads you get big perf wins. For retrieval/embedding heavy pipelines, batching and locality matter — you'd see better throughput on Dedicated because you can tune batch windows and the runtime for your seq lengths.
[03:10] Tom Reeves: mmh, will we need to run any infra on our side? Or is there a proxy? We want Egress control and VPC peering might be needed.
[03:20] Maya Chen: for Hosted you call the public API; for a more secure setup we offer Private (VPC peering or on-prem package). Dedicated can be offered in your VPC as well depending on contract. We can share the VPC peering diagram.
[03:35] Aisha Patel: SOC2 and ISO — do you have those attested?
[03:42] Ivy Park: yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and we have ISO 27001, will send the security pack after the call.
[03:50] Riley: oh great. Any penalties/SLAs for dedicated? We need 99.9 availability for the pilot.
[03:58] Leo Garcia: Dedicated has SLA tiers; 99.9 is achievable with Reserved capacity + failover policies. We also do automatic fallback to a smaller model variant if capacity is constrained, but obviously that changes latency/quality tradeoffs.
[04:20] Samir Das: pricing — I want a sense ballpark: how much more for Dedicated?
[04:25] Maya Chen: ballpark — Hosted is pay-as-you-go, per-token. Dedicated is a combination of commit (monthly) plus lower per-token compute. We can send a sample pricing sheet based on your expected QPS and token mix.
[04:40] Tom Reeves: redeploying models — how do rollouts work? We need canary, A/B, rollback.
[04:47] Leo Garcia: console supports rollouts: canary percentages, A/B, automatic fallback rules, and tracing hooks for per-route metrics. You can pin a model version per route.
[05:00] Aisha Patel: let's say we want our dev teams to play with it first, get to tokens quickly, and then we will run a pilot for 2 weeks. What's a realistic flow?
[05:12] Maya Chen: we typically do: 1) provide sandbox with $X credits (we'll offer $2k for this pilot), 2) SDK + quickstart repo, 3) short benchmark plan from SE, 4) 2-week pilot where you test latency, throughput, and data-handling needs, then reconvene to decide Dedicated or Private.
[05:35] Riley: are there rate limits on sandbox? We don't want our tests throttled artificially.
[05:40] Leo Garcia: sandbox has nominal quota but we'll set it to cover benchmark runs for that period. If you need larger bursts we'll configure burst windows.
[05:50] Tom Reeves: what's the typical onboarding friction? SSO? Roles?
[05:55] Ivy Park: we support SSO (SAML/OIDC), SSO provisioning, RBAC, token scopes. We'll send SSO integration guide.
[06:05] Samir Das: on the security docs — can you redact examples of logs with customer data? We need to know what is logged.
[06:12] Ivy Park: yes, we'll include audit log examples and log retention policy. Hosted retains request logs short-term; Dedicated/Private have configurable retention.
[06:22] Aisha Patel: ok good. On technical fit: our query patterns are spiky, mostly embeddings at night but chat during business hours. We worried about tail latency.
[06:35] Leo Garcia: for spiky workloads Dedicated with burst capacity is designed for that. Also, our smart routing can route by region and cost tier to keep P95 low. For strict tail latency you can pin to reserved nodes.
[06:55] Riley: any gotchas for embeddings specifically? Accuracy regressions post-quantization?
[07:02] Leo Garcia: embeddings are sensitive to quantization sometimes; we provide quantization profiles per-model and recommendations. For critical accuracy you can run evals and we'll recommend not to quantize or use a specific fp16 path.
[07:20] Tom Reeves: we use private datasets and need data residency in EU. Is that supported on Hosted?
[07:30] Maya Chen: Hosted has region controls; EU region is supported, but for strict residency Dedicated/Private is recommended so you control data egress.
[07:42] Aisha Patel: timeframe — if we like the sandbox, how quickly can we ramp to Dedicated?
[07:50] Maya Chen: typically 2–4 weeks for provisioning Dedicated after contract signing, less if you already have required networking in place. Private on-prem can take longer based on environment.
[08:05] Samir Das: can SE run a quick benchmark against our sample workload?
[08:10] Leo Garcia: yep, if you share a sample prompt set and data shapes we'll run a runbook and return P95/P99 guidance.
[08:20] Riley: what's the data path exactly — does Redwood store embeddings, or can we opt out?
[08:28] Ivy Park: you can opt-out of retention, and for Dedicated/Private you control persistence. Hosted by default keeps request logs for support but you can opt into shorter retention.
[08:40] Tom Reeves: okay good. Any mention of costs for support or premium SLAs?
[08:45] Maya Chen: enterprise support is priced separately — premium SLAs, longer observability retention, and faster incident response. We'll include support tiers in the pricing sheet.
[08:55] Aisha Patel: what about SDKs — we use Python and Go — are they fully supported?
[09:00] Leo Garcia: yes Python, Go, JS SDKs, plus curl examples. We have a sample repo for ingestion and vector indexing.
[09:10] Riley: any known differences between model variants that could affect us? e.g., smaller variants for cheaper inference.
[09:18] Leo Garcia: smaller variants trade quality for latency/cost — we offer Redwood-verified perf profiles so you can pick by perf/quality. We'll share the model catalog and perf matrix.
[09:30] Samir Das: how do you handle fallback — let's say a model is slow or unavailable, what's the behavior?
[09:36] Leo Garcia: fallback policies can route to a cheaper model or a smaller sequence length; there's also automatic retry/backoff and you can configure graceful degradation in the console.
[09:48] Tom Reeves: any compliance for regulated industries? e.g., healthcare PHI handling?
[09:55] Ivy Park: we have specific compliance packages available; for PHI workloads Private or Dedicated with strict KMS and audit configuration is recommended. We'll attach the compliance pack.
[10:05] Aisha Patel: cool — let's talk next steps. We'll want the sandbox, the security docs, and the benchmark template. Also a follow-up to discuss Dedicated sizing if the pilot looks good.
[10:20] Maya Chen: perfect. I'll send the sandbox invite and credits after the call, Leo will send the benchmark template in the next 48 hours, Ivy will attach SOC2 and SSO docs. We'll schedule a 45-minute follow-up in a week.
[10:35] Riley: quick Q — any advice for minimizing token cost for RAG workflows?
[10:40] Leo Garcia: practical tips: precompute embeddings for static content, aggressive caching of prompts/prefixes, use shorter context windows for low-value queries; Redwood Optimize can give recommendations based on traces.
[10:57] Samir Das: who on your side will be our main contact for the pilot?
[11:00] Maya Chen: it'll be me for commercial, Leo for the SE work, Ivy for onboarding/support.
[11:10] Tom Reeves: ok thanks all, sounds good.
[11:15] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the items. Have a good one.
[11:20] (call ends)

References: quickstart repo link (sent), security pack (to be sent), benchmark template (to be sent).
